## Why This Is Asked

This question probes system design at scale, covering data modeling, ingestion pipelines, delivery guarantees, ordering, and observability in a globally distributed, low-latency context.

## Key Concepts

- Event sourcing and durable logs (Kafka/Kinesis)
- Idempotent processing and deduplication
- Region-local vs global ordering
- Delivery guarantees (at-least-once vs exactly-once)
- Observability, testing, and chaos engineering

```javascript
// Example: idempotent publish wrapper
function publishAnnouncement(store, event) {

  if (store.has(id)) return; // dedup
  store.set(id, event);
  // emit to downstream
}
```

```python
# Pseudo vector clock merge for conflict resolution
from typing import Dict

def merge_vc(vc1: Dict[str,int], vc2: Dict[str,int]) -> Dict[str,int]:
```

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world KCNA deployments must protect data across tenants; this question probes envelope encryption design, key lifecycle, and how to audit and delete data without breaking consistency.

## Key Concepts
- Envelope encryption
- Per-tenant KEK/DEK lifecycle
- Key rotation with zero-downtime re-encryption
- Auditability and tenant-scoped deletion

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode for decrypting payload using tenant DEK
const wrappedDek = metadata.getTenantWrappedDek(tenantId);
const dek = kms.unwrapDek(tenantId, wrappedDek);
const plaintext = crypto.decrypt(payload, dek);
```

## Code Example

```javascript
class IdempotentProcessor {

  async onEvent(e) {
    if (await this.store.has(e.eventId)) return
    await this.store.put(e.eventId, true, TTL_MS)
    await writeLedger(e.userId, e.payload)
    commitOffsets()
  }
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical multitenant QoS design under bursty traffic and storms.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant rate limiting with token buckets
- Deficit Round Robin (DRR) scheduling
- Backpressure signaling and per-tenant buffers
- Observability: tail latency, SLA guards, isolation proofs

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo token bucket limiter
class TokenBucket { constructor(rate, burst) { this.rate = rate; this.burst = burst; this.tokens = burst; this.last = Date.now(); }
  consume(n) { this.refill(); if (this.tokens >= n) { this.tokens -= n; return true; } return false; }
  refill() { const now = Date.now(); const add = ((now - this.last) / 1000) * this.rate; this.tokens = Math.min(this.burst, this.tokens + add); this.last = now; }
}
```

- How do you detect and mitigate misbehaving tenants without impacting others?
